title: Nightly web error check
subtitle: Last night's web server log becomes an error report per endpoint, and an email to on-call if too many requests failed.

scenes.title: Bring in the tools
scenes.narration: Everything this script needs is built into Python: pattern matching for log lines, counting, JSON files and sending email.

scenes.title: Read the settings
scenes.narration: The script knows where the log and the report live, who is on call, and its alarm threshold: an email goes out when more than 5% of requests fail.

scenes.title: Open last night's log
scenes.narration: The access log is opened and read line by line. A different log file can be passed on the command line.

inputs.label: access.log
inputs.sublabel: logs/access.log, or the path given on the command line

code.snippet:
def main(path=LOG_PATH):
    with open(path) as fh:
        rows = summarize(parse(fh))
    with open(REPORT_PATH, "w") as out:
        json.dump(rows, out, indent=2)
    total = sum(r["requests"] for r in rows)
    errors = sum(r["errors"] for r in rows)
    rate = errors / total if total else 0
    if rate > ERROR_RATE_ALERT:
        send_alert(rows, rate)
    return rate

outputs.label: fh
outputs.detail: The file is streamed, so even a very large log is never loaded all at once.

scenes.title: Pick out the useful parts of each line
scenes.narration: Each line is matched against the log pattern to pull out the method, path and status code. Lines that don't fit the pattern are skipped quietly.

scenes.title: Count requests and failures per endpoint
scenes.narration: Requests are tallied per endpoint. Any status of 500 or above counts as a failure, and each endpoint gets its own error rate.

children.title: Treat /orders/123 and /orders/456 as one
children.narration: Numeric ids and query strings are stripped from each path, so the same endpoint is counted together instead of as thousands of separate URLs.

scenes.title: Save the error report
scenes.narration: The per-endpoint table is saved as a JSON report, busiest endpoints first.

scenes.title: Work out the overall failure rate
scenes.narration: All requests and all failures are added up across endpoints to get one failure rate for the night. An empty log counts as zero.

scenes.title: Decide whether to wake someone up
scenes.narration: If more than 5% of requests failed, the on-call engineer gets an email. Otherwise the script finishes quietly with just the report.

branch.question: Did more than 5% of requests fail?

scenes.title: Email the on-call engineer
scenes.narration: The email names the failure rate in its subject and lists the five endpoints with the most errors, sent through the internal mail server.

code.snippet:
def send_alert(rows, rate):
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["Subject"] = f"Error rate {rate:.1%} in last night's traffic"
    msg["To"] = ONCALL
    msg["From"] = "logbot@example.com"
    worst = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r["errors"], reverse=True)[:5]
    msg.set_content("\n".join(f'{r["endpoint"]}: {r["errors"]} errors' for r in worst))
    with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST) as s:
        s.send_message(msg)

outputs.label: oncall@example.com
outputs.detail: Subject: 'Error rate N% in last night's traffic'. Body: the five worst endpoints and their error counts.

summary.headline: Every night, a raw log becomes an error report per endpoint, and an email when failures pass 5%.
